mainTopic: The penalty for skipping a מומחה, payment by a non-expert, and when a judge must pay for a mistaken ruling
overview: The amud opens by proving from the משנה's own wording that רבי מאיר forbids a בכור slaughtered without a מומחה as a קנס, not because of doubt. The גמרא then asks whether every eye blemish changes after death, which decides whether witnesses about such a blemish can be trusted. A report from רבי יאשיה of אושא shows that only some change. Next, a non-expert whose ruling led to a בכור being slaughtered must pay: a quarter of the value for a small animal and half for a large one, because of the decree against raising small animals. A new משנה rules that a judge who errs must pay, unless he is a מומחה לבית דין. The גמרא explains that this applies when he caused the loss with his own hand. In the story of רבי טרפון and the cow whose womb was removed, רבי עקיבא tells him he is exempt, both because his error went against a משנה and because he is a court expert. The amud ends with a new משנה: a paid examiner of בכורות cannot be relied on unless he is a מומחה. Its explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports the penalty reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה's own words, 'since it was slaughtered not by a מומחה,' mean רבי מאיר is giving a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה itself is precise in supporting this. רבי מאיר says: Since it was slaughtered without an expert, it is forbidden. Learn from this that רבי מאיר is imposing a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the exact wording of the משנה for what רבה בר בר חנה said earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not say 'because maybe the blemish was not real.' He says 'since it was slaughtered without a מומחה,' which blames the person's behavior. That points to a קנס for skipping the expert. It does not point to a doubt about the blemish, because body blemishes do not change after death.

keyTerms.meaning: is precise; its exact wording proves the point
since; because
an expert authorized to judge blemishes on a בכור
a penalty (a rabbinic fine or prohibition)
imposes a penalty

steps.whyThisMatters: The animal is forbidden as a punishment for skipping the מומחה. The blemish itself is not in doubt, so the reason is not uncertainty.

phrases.english: The Mishnah is also precise (in supporting this),
phrases.notes: Supports רבה בר בר חנה's earlier explanation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.english: Since it was slaughtered not by the ruling of an expert, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The reason given is the person's conduct, not doubt about the blemish.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קְנָסָא קָא קָנֵיס רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Learn from this that Rabbi Meir is imposing a penalty,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה בר בר חנה's statement from the previous section of the daf: the dispute concerns body blemishes, and רבי מאיר forbids as a קנס.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי מאיר's prohibition is a קנס, not a doubt
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה: 'הואיל ונשחט שלא על פי מומחה'

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms the proof: the משנה should be understood as רבה בר בר חנה explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it. (The proof stands.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section by accepting the proof from the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'שמע מינה' at the end mean no one challenges the proof. רבה בר בר חנה's reading is now settled: רבי מאיר forbids a body blemish as a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, a בכור slaughtered without a מומחה is forbidden as a קנס. This applies even for a body blemish, where nothing is actually in doubt.

phrases.english: Learn from it (it is proven).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms and seals the proof from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה supports רבה בר בר חנה: רבי מאיר's prohibition is a קנס.

steps.title: Do all eye blemishes change after death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'because they change' means every eye blemish changes after death, or only some.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: When it says 'because of those that change,' does it mean that all of them change? Or perhaps some change and some do not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the reason given for eye blemishes. It wants to know whether every eye blemish changes after death or only some.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, eye blemishes were treated differently from body blemishes 'because they change' after death. That phrase can be read two ways. Either changing is guaranteed for every eye, or it is only a possibility, so some eyes stay the same.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised before them (the Sages)
those that change
or perhaps
there are; there exists

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
'Because of those that change' —
phrases.notes: Quotes the reason given earlier for eye blemishes.

phrases.english: does it mean that all of them change,
or perhaps there are some that change
and there are some that do not change?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the 'because they change' reason mentioned earlier on the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether every eye blemish changes after death, or only some

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference this question makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask why the question matters in practice. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way, eye blemishes are already forbidden after slaughter. So the גמרא needs to show a real case where the two readings lead to different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical relevance of the question in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two possibilities lead to different rulings

steps.title: The difference: whether we trust witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether we believe witnesses who say the eye blemish looked the same while the animal was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is about contradicting witnesses. If all eye blemishes change, the witnesses are liars. If some change and some do not, we rely on them. So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical difference: can we trust witnesses who testify that the blemish was there, looking just like this, before the slaughter? Then it asks again which reading is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every eye changes after death, the eye now cannot look the way it did in life. Anyone who says 'it looked exactly like this' is clearly lying. If only some eyes change, their testimony is possible, so the court can rely on them and the animal may be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: to contradict; to show to be false
witnesses
liars
we rely

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether eye blemishes are real blemishes. It is about whether witnesses can believably say the eye looked the same before death.

phrases.english: For contradicting witnesses.
phrases.notes: Witnesses who say the blemish looked like this while the animal was alive.

phrases.english: If you say: all of them change —
then they (the witnesses) are liars,
and if you say: there are some that change
and there are some that do not change —
we rely on them.
So what is the answer?
phrases.notes: Returns to the question from step 3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by showing the practical difference, then reopens the question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether witnesses who say the eye looked the same in life are believed (some change) or called liars (all change).

steps.title: רבי יאשיה offers to show the eye membranes that change
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports that רבי יאשיה of אושא told him, 'Come and I will show you the eye membranes that change.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבה בר בר חנה said: רבי יאשיה from אושא told me, 'Come and I will show you the eye membranes that change.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report from רבה בר בר חנה to answer the question. This step quotes the source, and the next step will draw the lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה offered to point out particular eye membranes that change after death. The exact wording of his offer will be the key to answering the question.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a proof)
told; related
come and I will show you
the membranes or corneas of the eye

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׂח לִי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya of Usha told me,
'Come and I will show you the eye membranes that change.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question restated at the end of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Whether all eye membranes change or only some
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה's report of what רבי יאשיה of אושא said

steps.title: The inference: some change and some do not
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יאשיה had to show which membranes change, it follows that some change and some do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said to him 'Come and I will show you,' we can infer that some change and some do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רבי יאשיה's words: only some eye membranes change. This answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every eye changed, there would be nothing special to point out. Offering to show 'the ones that change' means they are a specific group, set apart from others that stay the same. So witnesses who say the eye looked the same in life are not automatically liars.

keyTerms.meaning: since he said to him
by implication; it follows that

steps.whatToRemember: Not every eye blemish changes after death. Some do and some do not, so witnesses who say an eye blemish existed in life can be relied on.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question in step 3. Witnesses who testify that an eye blemish was there before slaughter are not automatically rejected.

phrases.english: Since he said to him 'Come and I will show you,'
it follows that there are some that change
and there are some that do not change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the source quoted in step 6, answering the question from steps 3 and 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Some eye membranes change after death and some do not, so witnesses about an eye blemish are not automatically considered liars.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a non-expert who examined a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה it is about to discuss: a non-expert examined a בכור, it was slaughtered on his word, it must be buried, and he pays from his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone who is not an expert examined a firstborn animal, and it was slaughtered because of what he said, the animal must be buried, and he must pay from his own money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next question about whose opinion this line follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור with a blemish may only be slaughtered and eaten if an expert, a מומחה, approved the blemish. Here a non-expert approved it, so the meat is forbidden and must be buried. The non-expert caused the כהן a loss, so he has to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert authorized to judge blemishes
A firstborn animal that belongs to the כהן
It must be buried, because it is forbidden
From his own money

phrases.english: One who is not an expert,
and he examined the firstborn,
and it was slaughtered on his word,
this animal must be buried,
and he must pay from his own money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּמְחֶה, וְרָאָה אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of eye blemishes that change, to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור slaughtered on a non-expert's word is buried, and the non-expert pays.

steps.title: Does this unattributed משנה follow only רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that since the משנה forbids the animal outright, the unattributed משנה seems to follow רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that we learned this unattributed משנה according to רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders whether this anonymous משנה follows only one side of a מחלוקת, namely רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids any בכור that was slaughtered without an expert's approval. Others allow it if the blemish can still be checked after slaughter. Because the משנה simply says 'it must be buried,' it sounds like רבי מאיר alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say, a suggestion the גמרא will test
An unattributed, anonymous משנה
The תנא who forbids the animal in every case

phrases.english: Shall we say we learned an unattributed משנה
according to רבי מאיר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the quoted משנה follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the משנה limited to רבי מאיר's view?

steps.title: No, it may be about eye membranes, where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The משנה may refer to a blemish on the eye membranes, which changes after death, so everyone agrees the animal is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the case is a blemish on the membranes of the eye, and then everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that the משנה follows only רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned in Step 7 that some eye membranes change after death. If the blemish was there, nobody can check it properly after slaughter. So even the Sages who argue with רבי מאיר would agree the animal must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, a word used to reject a suggestion
The membranes of the eye
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can fit everyone's view if it is about an eye blemish that changes after death.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is about the membranes of the eye,
and then it is everyone's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in Step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה is only רבי מאיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be limited to a blemish that cannot be checked after death

steps.title: A ברייתא on how much the non-expert pays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the non-expert pays a quarter of the value for a small animal and half for a large animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when he pays, he pays a quarter for a small animal and half for a large animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the amount of the payment mentioned in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'he pays.' The ברייתא adds that he does not pay the full value. He pays a quarter for a sheep or goat and half for an ox.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
One quarter
A small animal, like a sheep or goat
A large animal, like an ox

phrases.english: It was taught:
When he pays, he pays
a quarter for a small animal,
and half for a large animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the payment mentioned in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quarter of the value for a small animal, half for a large one.

steps.title: Why the difference between small and large animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the payment is different for small and large animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the different amounts. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the non-expert caused a loss either way, why should the share he pays change with the type of animal? The גמרא wants the logic.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a quarter for small animals but half for large ones

steps.title: רב פפא: a large loss versus a small loss
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that losing an ox is a big loss, while losing a sheep or goat is a small loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this one is a big loss, and that one is a small loss.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the amount depends on how big the loss is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox is worth much more, so the כהן loses more. For that reason the non-expert pays a bigger share of it.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who answers
A big loss
A small loss

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
This one is a big loss,
and that one is a small loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זֶה הֶפְסֵד מְרוּבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The share depends on the size of the loss

steps.title: Then just pay according to the actual loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. If the issue is the size of the loss, the same fraction already gives a bigger payment for the more valuable animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let him pay according to the loss!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A quarter of an ox's value is already much more money than a quarter of a sheep's value. So paying the same fraction for both would already match the size of the loss. Raising the fraction to half for an ox does not follow from רב פפא's logic.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, used to introduce a challenge
According to the loss

phrases.english: If so,
let him pay according to the loss!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reason of a big loss versus a small loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the same fraction already scales with the loss, so a different fraction is not explained

steps.title: The reason is the decree on raising small animals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר מנוח, in the name of רב אחא בר איקא, says the Sages lowered the payment for small animals because of the decree against raising them in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר מנוח said in the name of רב אחא בר איקא: because of the decree against people who raise small animals, the Sages touched on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new reason is given for the lower payment on small animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small animals damage fields, so the Sages limited where they could be raised in ארץ ישראל. Because of this decree, a small בכור is worth less to the כהן, or more of a burden. So the Sages reduced the payment to a quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
A rabbinic decree
People who raise small animals
They touched on it, meaning the Sages adjusted the amount

steps.whatToRemember: The quarter payment for small animals comes from the decree on raising small animals, not only from the size of the loss.

phrases.english: רב הונא בר מנוח said
in the name of רב אחא בר איקא:
because of the decree against those who raise small animals
they touched on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר מָנוֹחַ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 14 with a new reason
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reason with a different one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fractions come only from the size of the loss
steps.terutzMaskana: The quarter for small animals comes from the decree about raising them

steps.title: New משנה: a judge who rules wrongly
steps.stepSummary: A judge who ruled wrongly about money or about טומאה and טהרה: his ruling stands, but he pays from his own money. A judge who is a recognized court expert does not pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a judge judged a case and cleared the guilty, made the innocent liable, called something pure impure, or called something impure pure, what he did stands, and he pays from his own money. If he was an expert for the court, he does not have to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, moving from blemishes to judges who make mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as the non-expert with the בכור. A judge who caused a loss through a mistake must pay. An authorized court expert is exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
He cleared the guilty party
What he did stands
An expert recognized by the court
Exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the main source for when a judge has to pay for a mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he judged a case,
cleared the liable party
or made the innocent party liable,
declared the pure impure
or declared the impure pure,
what he did stands,
and he pays from his own money.
And if he was an expert for the court,
he is exempt from paying.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּן אֶת הַדִּין, זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about mistaken judges
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mistaken judge's ruling stands and he pays, unless he is a court expert.

steps.title: Does the משנה follow only רבי מאיר on indirect damage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the unattributed משנה, which makes a mistaken judge pay, follows רבי מאיר's view that a person is liable for indirectly caused damage (דינא דגרמי).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Should we say that the unattributed משנה was taught according to רבי מאיר, who holds people liable for indirectly caused damage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts analyzing the משנה. It wonders if the rule that a mistaken judge pays only works according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge's ruling seems to cause loss only indirectly, since he only spoke words. Making someone pay for indirect damage is the view of רבי מאיר (דינא דגרמי). The גמרא would rather not say that an unattributed משנה (סתם משנה) follows only one side of a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test)
an unattributed teaching, with no name attached
liability for damage caused indirectly
the תנא who holds people liable for indirect damage

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on the previous משנה

phrases.english: Shall we say we learned the unattributed Mishnah like Rabbi Meir,
who rules liability for indirectly caused damage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which תנא the משנה in Step 16 follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the judge's liability depend on רבי מאיר's view of דינא דגרמי?

steps.title: The judge acted directly with his own hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא in the name of רב explains that the משנה is speaking of a judge who physically took the item and handed it over. That makes it direct damage, so everyone agrees he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רב: The משנה means a case where the judge took the item and handed it over with his own hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the משנה does not need רבי מאיר. The judge did more than speak: he physically moved the money himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the judge personally hands the item over, he is a direct damager, not just an indirect cause. Liability for direct damage is accepted by everyone. So the משנה fits all opinions, not only רבי מאיר's.

keyTerms.meaning: for example; the case is one where
took and gave with his hand, meaning he physically moved the item

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for the rest of the sugya: a mistaken judge pays only when he acted physically. Every following case is explained in this way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said in the name of Rav:
For example, where he took and gave with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by redefining the case as direct damage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The judge's liability depends on דינא דגרמי, which only רבי מאיר accepts
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge physically handed over the item, so this is direct damage that everyone agrees requires payment

steps.title: How does 'acting by hand' fit wrongly freeing someone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's explanation. It works when the judge wrongly makes an innocent person pay, but when he wrongly frees a liable person he just says 'you are exempt.' Nothing is handed over.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense when he made the innocent party liable: he took and handed over with his hand. But when he exempted the liable party, how could that happen? If he just told him 'You are exempt,' then he did not take and give with his hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב's answer against the other half of the משנה and finds a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a judge wrongly frees a debtor, the usual outcome is that he only speaks: 'You don't owe.' No money moves, so there is no direct physical act. That would bring back the problem of indirect damage.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, this part makes sense
but (introduces the difficult part)
what is the case? how does it work?
but look, the fact is

phrases.english: Granted, where he made the innocent party liable,
it is where he took and gave with his hand;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב הֵיכִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: but where he exempted the liable party, what is the case?
If he said to him 'You are exempt,'
but he did not take and give with his hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 18's explanation covers every case in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that the judge acted with his hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wrongly freeing someone normally involves only words, so no physical act happened

steps.title: רבינא: the judge took back the collateral
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the creditor was holding collateral (משכון). The judge physically took it from him and returned it to the debtor, which is a direct act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case is where the lender had collateral, and the judge took it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finds a way the judge could have acted with his hand even when freeing a debtor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender already held the borrower's collateral. By physically removing it and giving it back, the judge directly caused the lender's loss. So the 'by hand' explanation works here too.

keyTerms.meaning: collateral or pledge held by a lender
and he took it from him

phrases.english: Ravina said:
For example, where he (the lender) had collateral
and he (the judge) took it from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Freeing a debtor is only words, so it is indirect
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge physically took the collateral from the lender, so it is direct damage

steps.title: Direct action in the purity cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the judge acted with his own hand in the טומאה cases. To declare a pure item טמא, he touched it to a שרץ. To declare an impure item טהור, he mixed it into the owner's pure produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He declared the pure impure: he touched them to a creeping creature. He declared the impure pure: he mixed them in with the owner's produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the 'by hand' rule to the second half of the משנה, about טומאה and טהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the judge physically caused the loss. Touching the item to a שרץ made it truly טמא. Mixing impure produce into pure produce spoiled the whole mix once the true status became known. So he is a direct damager in these cases too.

keyTerms.meaning: he declared a pure item impure
he declared an impure item pure
a creeping creature whose carcass makes things טמא
he mixed them

steps.confusionAlert: In the second case the judge did not make anything impure by touching. The loss comes from mixing: the owner's pure produce was combined with impure produce, so the whole mixture became a problem.
steps.whatToRemember: A mistaken judge pays only when he caused the loss with his own hand. Examples: handing over the money, taking back collateral, touching an item to a שרץ, or mixing impure produce into pure produce.

phrases.english: He declared the pure impure:
where he made a creeping creature touch them;
he declared the impure pure:
where he mixed them with his (the owner's) produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר דְּאַגַּע בְּהוּ שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends Step 18's principle to the טומאה and טהרה cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ruling about purity is only words and cannot be direct damage
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge physically touched the item to a שרץ or mixed the produce, which is direct damage

steps.title: רבי טרפון and the cow whose womb was removed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה tells a story. A cow had its womb removed. רבי טרפון ruled it a טריפה and it was fed to dogs. The חכמים in יבנה later ruled it was permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There was an incident with a cow whose womb was removed. רבי טרפון fed it to the dogs. The case came before the חכמים in יבנה, and they permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a real-life case of a mistaken ruling. It sets up the question of whether רבי טרפון must pay for the cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון treated the missing womb as making the cow a טריפה, so it was thrown to the dogs. The חכמים ruled that such a cow is kosher. This makes רבי טרפון's ruling a mistake that caused a loss, which connects directly to the rule about a judge's liability that came just before.

keyTerms.meaning: the משנה
here: the womb
a תנא who ruled on the case
the town where the Sages' court sat after the Temple's destruction
and they permitted it

steps.confusionAlert: Here הָאֵם does not mean 'its mother.' It means the cow's womb (uterus) was removed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story tests the rule from the earlier משנה. The question is whether an expert like רבי טרפון must pay for a mistaken ruling. The משנה continues with that discussion.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
And there was an incident with a cow whose womb was removed,
and Rabbi Tarfon fed it to the dogs,
and the incident came before the Sages in Yavneh,
and they permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a story that applies the rule about a judge's liability
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow whose womb was removed is permitted, against רבי טרפון's ruling that it was a טריפה

steps.title: The doctor's evidence that a cow without a womb can live
steps.stepSummary: תודוס הרופא testifies that cows and pigs leaving Alexandria always have their wombs removed. These animals live normally, so removing the womb does not make an animal a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And תודוס הרופא said: No cow or pig leaves Alexandria of Egypt unless they cut out its womb, so that it cannot give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the story and brings proof that the חכמים in יבנה were right. A doctor reports that animals regularly live without a womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is an animal with an injury it cannot survive. The Egyptians removed the wombs of their prize animals so no one else could breed them, and these animals lived long, healthy lives. So removing the womb is not a fatal injury, and the cow was kosher all along.

keyTerms.meaning: תודוס (Theodosius) the doctor
Literally 'mother'; here it means the womb
They cut / remove
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This evidence proves that רבי טרפון's ruling was a real mistake. That sets up the question of whether he has to pay for the cow that was fed to the dogs.

phrases.english: And Todos the doctor said:
No cow or pig goes out
from Alexandria of Egypt
unless they cut out its womb,
phrases.notes: Literally 'that they do not cut', meaning 'without cutting'.

phrases.english: so that it will not give birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the factual basis for the חכמים in יבנה permitting the cow in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That a cow whose womb was removed is not a טריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The doctor's report that Alexandrian animals live normally after their wombs are removed.

steps.title: רבי טרפון fears he must pay
steps.stepSummary: Once he realizes his ruling was wrong, רבי טרפון says, 'Your donkey is gone, Tarfon,' meaning he expects to sell his donkey to pay the owner back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: Your donkey is gone, Tarfon!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון reacts to the news that he caused a loss by ruling wrongly. This sets up רבי עקיבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון assumes a judge who wrongly causes someone to lose property has to pay for it. Because the cow was fed to dogs on his word, he thinks he owes its value.

keyTerms.meaning: Your donkey is gone, meaning 'I will have to pay with my own property'

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
Your donkey is gone, Tarfon!
phrases.notes: He expects to sell his donkey to pay damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the money consequence from the proof that his ruling was wrong.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון assumes he is liable to pay for the cow he wrongly declared a טריפה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a court-approved expert does not pay
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא tells רבי טרפון that since he is a recognized expert for the court, he is exempt from paying for his mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: רבי טרפון, you are an expert for the court, and anyone who is an expert for the court is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא calms רבי טרפון and gives the final ruling of the משנה: he does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge who is officially recognized as an expert (מומחה לבית דין) is protected from paying for honest mistakes in judgment. This matches the earlier rule in the פרק about expert judges.

keyTerms.meaning: A judge officially recognized as an expert by the court or the public
Exempt from paying

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ruling: a recognized expert judge who rules wrongly does not have to pay for the loss.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, אַתָּה מוּמְחֶה לְבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon, you are an expert for the court,
and anyone who is an expert for the court
is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טרפון's worry from Step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מומחה לבית דין who errs is exempt from paying.

steps.title: Why not say the ruling was simply cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא needed the expert-judge reason. רבי טרפון erred against an explicit משנה, and such a ruling is automatically cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But derive it from the fact that he erred in a matter stated in a משנה, and one who errs in a matter stated in a משנה, the ruling is reversed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges רבי עקיבא's reasoning. It suggests a simpler, stronger reason he should have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה (חולין) already states that an animal without a womb is kosher. A ruling that contradicts an explicit משנה is an obvious error, so it has no force and is simply reversed. In that case, the owner who fed the cow to the dogs relied on an invalid ruling, so why mention the expert exemption at all?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him derive it from [another reason]
Erred in something stated explicitly in a משנה
The ruling is reversed / cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: 'Mistake in a משנה' does not mean a small error. It means the judge ruled against a clear, written law, so his ruling counts as if it never happened.

phrases.english: Gemara:
But derive it from the fact that he erred in a matter stated in a Mishnah,
and one who errs in a matter stated in a Mishnah, the ruling is reversed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason רבי עקיבא gave in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's choice of the מומחה לבית דין reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler reason exists: an error against an explicit משנה is void. That should make the expert exemption unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא meant 'one reason, and another besides.' First, the error was against a משנה and is void. Second, even if it was only an error of judgment, an expert is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying one reason and another. One: one who errs in a matter stated in a משנה, the ruling is reversed. And another: even if you erred in reasoning, you are an expert for the court, and anyone who is an expert for the court is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying רבי עקיבא really meant both reasons. He only spelled out the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one fits the actual case: the ruling went against a משנה, so it is cancelled. Reason two adds that even if this were only a mistake in weighing opinions (שיקול הדעת), a recognized expert would still be exempt. So רבי טרפון is free from paying either way.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying one reason, and another as well
An error in weighing opinions or reasoning, not against an explicit law
Alternatively / even if

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון is exempt for two reasons. His ruling contradicted a משנה, so it is void. And even an error in judgment by a מומחה לבית דין does not require payment.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:
One: one who errs in a matter stated in a Mishnah, the ruling is reversed,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד — אִי נָמֵי בְּשִׁיקּוּל הַדַּעַת טָעִיתָה,
phrases.english: and another: even if you erred in reasoning,
you are an expert for the court,
and anyone who is an expert for the court
is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the speaker's words as containing two layered reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא relied only on the expert exemption and ignored the simpler 'error in a משנה' reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא held both reasons. The 'error in a משנה' reason is primary, and the expert exemption is added in case the error was only one of judgment.

steps.title: A paid examiner of firstborns is not relied upon unless he is an expert
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a person takes payment to examine בכורות for blemishes, we may not slaughter a בכור based on his ruling, unless he is a recognized מומחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person takes payment to be the one who examines firstborn animals, we may not slaughter a firstborn based on what he says, unless he is a recognized expert.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new rule. A paid examiner of בכורות cannot permit their slaughter unless he is a מומחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be slaughtered after someone rules that it has a real, permanent blemish (מום). This משנה says that we may not slaughter based on the ruling of someone who takes payment for it. The reason is not given on this amud; the continuation of the משנה and the גמרא on the next amud discuss it. The one exception is a recognized expert, which matches the theme of the previous story, where expert status changed the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה.
One who takes payment or a fee.
Firstborn kosher animals. They may be slaughtered only if they have a blemish.
Based on his word or ruling.
A recognized expert, whose authority the court accepts.

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a basic halachic principle: a person who is paid to give a ruling has a problem with his ruling. A recognized מומחה is treated differently, and the rest of the משנה and the גמרא will explain why.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the examiner is a bad person or that the animal is forbidden forever. It only says we cannot slaughter based on his ruling. Another qualified examiner could still look at the animal.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who takes payment
to be the one who examines the firstborn animals
phrases.notes: He checks whether they have a blemish that permits slaughter.

phrases.english: we may not slaughter based on his ruling
unless he was a recognized expert

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַנּוֹטֵל שָׂכָר לִהְיוֹת רוֹאֶה אֶת הַבְּכוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It continues the theme of the expert's special status seen in the רבי טרפון story (Steps 25-27).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A paid examiner of בכורות cannot permit slaughter by his ruling, unless he is a recognized מומחה.
